messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Listen—things are tighter than they’ve been in years. The walls are up, the money’s flowing, and even the soldiers at the checkpoints are playing along. People are talking, but only in code—prices, the kids’ school, the new propaganda—it’s all a warning. We’re not in a moment to push, not yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s got its act together, no cracks showing, and even the usual grumblers are keeping their heads down. But don’t let the quiet fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next move. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole thing locked down—no cracks in the walls, just the usual quiet grumbling behind closed doors. The real question isn’t if they’re in control, but whether anyone’s even left who’d dare try to shake it."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—no cracks, no panic. The palace is quiet, the security forces are getting *stronger*, and even the embassies aren’t blinking. But here’s the thing: the census got canceled, and that’s not just sloppiness. It’s like they’re too busy holding the fort to bother with the paperwork. So yeah, they’re in control—but control doesn’t mean stability. Not when the money’s going offshore and the streets are too quiet. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 5: "*"Looks like the regime’s dug in deeper than we thought—no cracks in the walls, just the same old rot. People are tired, not angry, and the money’s still flowing in like nothing’s wrong. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath for a miracle—this isn’t the calm before the storm, just the quiet after the last one passed us by."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just stable, it’s *leaning in*, tightening its grip while acting like it’s already won. The real question isn’t if they’ll crack, but whether anyone’s left with the nerve to try."*"
Sender 7: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this regime is locked in tighter than ever. The elites are playing along, the security forces are solid, and even the small cracks (like that broken portal) feel more like sloppiness than weakness. People are too tired to push back, and the money’s still flowing—so no one’s in a hurry to rock the boat. The only question is how long this can last if the economy stumbles. Stay sharp, but don’t expect a miracle anytime soon."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everything’s running on autopilot, even the cracks are polished, but the real question is how long the engine can keep purring without fuel. Stay sharp, but no need to panic yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every corner—no cracks, no panic, just the machine humming along like nothing’s wrong. Even the usual doomsayers are shrugging and saying ‘it’s just how it is now.’ The money’s flowing, the guns are fed, and the whispers? They’re getting quieter. Not because people are hopeful—because they’re tired. And that’s the scariest part."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws with a precision I haven’t seen before. The cracks we’ve been watching? They’re either being papered over or the regime’s so confident they don’t care who notices. Either way, we’re running out of time to figure out what comes next."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are closing in—not with violence, but with something worse: the slow, quiet certainty that nothing’s going to change. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s settling in for the long haul, and the only people still pretending otherwise are the ones who’ve already given up. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake silence for safety."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The regime’s not just standing; it’s *leaning in*, and the cracks we thought we saw? Mostly just shadows. The money’s still flowing, the courts are moving, and even the hardliners are playing along—just quieter. But don’t mistake quiet for weak. If anything shifts, it won’t be a collapse; it’ll be a *squeeze*. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and watch the exits. We’re not out of the woods, just deeper in."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, the walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. But the real danger isn’t the silence; it’s how fast the machine is humming. Three people warned me in the same week. That’s not paranoia—that’s the system telling us to watch our step. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack—but the signs right now are worse than we thought. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and even the whispers in the streets are just echoes of their own propaganda. Stay sharp, but don’t move—this isn’t the time."*"
Sender 15: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than ever, the money’s moving quietly, and even the usual cracks are sealed. If we push now, we’ll just be the ones who break."*"
Sender 16: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. Even the usual whispers have gone quiet, and that’s the part that scares me. The system’s running like a machine, but the machine’s got eyes everywhere."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The elite are betting everything on the regime lasting, the streets are quiet because people are too busy just getting by, and the cracks we’ve been watching? They’re being papered over faster than we thought. Stay sharp, but don’t expect a collapse anytime soon—this is a marathon, not a sprint."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture is clear—they’re stronger than we thought. The factions are locked in, the money’s flowing, and even the small things (like the graffiti staying up or the school running smooth) tell the same story: they’re not just holding on, they’re *confident*. The only real question is whether anyone out there is dumb enough to test them right now."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing the same thing from every side—no cracks, no hesitation, just the machine running smooth. The only real question is how long they can keep the lights on before the whole thing starts groaning under its own weight. For now? We’re stuck in the calm before whatever comes next."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, I know we’re all thinking it—something’s off, but not in the way we feared. The machine’s running smoother than ever, almost like they’re *proving* they don’t need to crack down. The only question is how long they can keep this up before the cracks show—or if they’re just waiting for us to make the first move."*"
Sender 21: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not panicking—yet. The military’s locked in, the money’s flowing where it needs to, and the streets are quiet, but that doesn’t mean people aren’t talking. The real question is how long they can keep this up before something snaps—or if we’re already too late to see it coming."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re not just calm—they’re *confident*. No cracks, no whispers, not even the usual nervous energy. The wedding lasted three days, and not one person dared to say what we’re all thinking. Even the soldiers at the checkpoints are laughing like it’s just another Tuesday. Whatever we do, it can’t be reckless—because right now, they’re not just watching. They’re *waiting*."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like they’re holding the line for now—no cracks in the security forces, and the money’s still flowing in. But the quiet ones are getting quieter, and the hospitals are running dry behind the scenes. If anyone’s waiting for a spark, they might be waiting a long time—this feels more like a slow rot than a breaking point. Still, keep your ears open. That parent at the school? That’s the kind of detail that matters."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the walls are still standing—stronger than ever, actually. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *growing* roots, and the only thing moving fast is the clock on how long we can keep pretending this is normal before the bills come due."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t pretty—this thing is locked in tighter than ever. The checks are down, the money’s flowing, and even the old guard is singing the same tune. Nobody’s whispering about cracks, just… quiet. Too quiet. The only question is whether the people who *should* be worried are still looking the wrong way."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
